q-105555.name: Question 1
q-105555.problem:
Consider the vector field $F=\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)\,i-y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,j+y{z}^{3}\,k.$ 
Find $∇\cdot F.$
q-105555.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
∇\cdot F=\text{div}\,F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy))+\frac{∂}{∂y}(-y\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(y{z}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3y{z}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector field F=ln⁡(xy)i−ycos⁡xj+yz3k. Find ∇⋅F.

a
1xy−cos⁡x+z3
b
1xyi−cos⁡xj+z3k
c
1x−cos⁡x+3yz2
d
1x+sin⁡x+3yz2
e
1yi−sin⁡xj+3yz2k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If F=Pi+Qj+Rk is a vector field on R3 and the partial derivatives of the components of F all exist, then the divergence of F is the scalar field given by

∇⋅F=divF=∂P∂x+∂Q∂y+∂R∂z.

Therefore, we have ∇⋅F=∂P∂x+∂Q∂y+∂R∂z=∂∂x(ln⁡(xy))+∂∂y(−ycos⁡x)+∂∂z(yz3)=1x−cos⁡x+3yz2.

q-105559.name: Question 2
q-105559.problem:
Consider the vector field $F=\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi x\,i+y\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi y\,j+{e}^{2z}\,k.$ 
Evaluate $∇\cdot F$ at the point $(0,1,0).$
q-105559.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j+R\,k$ is a vector field on ${R}^{3}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
∇\cdot F=\text{div}\,F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}+\frac{∂R}{∂z} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{2z}) \\  & =-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi x+\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi y+\pi y\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi y+2{e}^{2z}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(0,1,0),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\cdot F)(0,1,0) & =-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+2{e}^{0} \\  & =0+0-\pi +2 \\  & =2-\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

a

2−π
c
π

Correct
EXPLANATION

If F=Pi+Qj+Rk is a vector field on R3 and the partial derivatives of the components of F all exist, then the divergence of F is the scalar field given by

∇⋅F=divF=∂P∂x+∂Q∂y+∂R∂z.

q-105572.name: Question 3
q-105572.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114595/assets/584016c88e5916984e181118d52caab95dba1fd0d861e0fd248a4e023d1b07da.png)

Consider the vector field $F$ shown above. Which of the following statements are true everywhere in the domain of $F?$

- $\text{div}\,F=0$
- $\text{div}\,F>0$
- $\text{div}\,F<0$
- $F$ is solenoidal
q-105572.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{div}\,F=∇\cdot F$ denotes the divergence of the vector field $F.$

Intuitively, the divergence of $F$ at a point $P$ measures how much $F$ acts like a source or a sink at $P:$

- If $F$ acts like a source at $P,$ then $∇\cdot F>0$ at $P.$

- If $F$ acts like a sink at $P,$ then $∇\cdot F<0$ at $P.$

- If $F$ acts like neither a source nor a sink at $P,$ then $∇\cdot F=0$ at $P.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14114595/assets/6c747149618d4c5ef35e727af15cd001365bd9c2d5e064689baf24c6ee23cff9.png)

If $∇\cdot F=0$ everywhere in the domain of $F,$ we say that $F$ is solenoidal.

With that in mind, let's examine each statement:

- Statement III is true, whereas statements I and II are false. Notice that the lengths of the vectors decrease as we move horizontally and vertically towards the origin. Therefore, the vector field $F$ acts like a sink at every point.

- Statement IV is false. Since $∇\cdot F\ne 0,$ the vector field $F$ is not solenoidal.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

If ∇⋅F=0 everywhere in the domain of F, we say that F is solenoidal.
